hook.text: Everything you're about to hear was generated from the prompts shown, with no edits or modifications. Just 11v4.

summary.tone: Cinematic, minimal and confident: a calm off-white canvas with two-tone gradient orbs and point-cloud faces, letting playful, emotional generated performances (film set, news reader, phone call) carry the proof, closing on an understated aspirational line and wordmark.

signature_moments.description: Each voice demo shows the exact prompt (including bracketed audio tags like [voice breaking], [laughs], [checking]) as a two-line karaoke caption under a breathing point-cloud face, with words lighting up in sync with the generated speech.
signature_moments.why_premium: It turns the product claim into visible proof: the viewer reads the input while hearing the output, so the demo doubles as evidence and the restrained typography keeps it elegant rather than technical.

signature_moments.description: Abstract gradient-orb metaphors for each feature: the orb splits into equalizer pill tracks for 'tone', pixelates for 'texture', two outline circles merge via their filled intersection for 'speaker similarity', and a glowing core bursts into a multi-depth dot lattice for '100 languages'.
signature_moments.why_premium: Every feature gets a bespoke, on-brand motion idea timed to the spoken word instead of generic UI or bullet text, with grain, blur and zoom-through transitions keeping the whole piece one continuous camera move.

signature_moments.description: A camera sweep past a giant defocused 'v4' pulls back to a gradient 'V4' in an outline ring, which shrinks into the 'Eleven V4' pill lockup and resolves into the ElevenLabs wordmark with a gradient sweep.
signature_moments.why_premium: The end card is earned through continuous scale/focus changes that echo the badge from the opening disclaimer, bookending the film and landing the brand with a single sync point (impact-labelled SFX x099) rather than a static slate.

hook.evidence: Opens on a bold, verifiable claim that everything heard is unedited generated audio from the prompts shown, immediately followed by 'doesn't just speak, it performs' and a dramatic demo; the first 8 s are text on a plain field, so the visual grab is quieter than the verbal one.

clarity.evidence: One idea per beat: performance/audio tags, professional voice clones with better similarity, long-form consistency, 100 languages, and a low-latency Turbo variant, each followed or preceded by an audible demo. Feature lines are only spoken (apart from 'Intent.' and 'v4 Turbo'), and there is no availability/pricing information.

ui_showcase.evidence: No product UI appears anywhere; the 'product' is shown through prompt captions and abstract visuals, so a UI showcase score does not apply.

motion_polish.evidence: Rotating point-cloud faces, orb morphs (split, pill tracks, pixelate, concentric orbits), intersecting-circle fill, zoom-through bridges, word-synced karaoke captions and a multi-stage logo resolve, all with consistent grain and blur and almost no hard cuts.

sound_design.evidence: Judged from anchor audio facts plus visuals: 102 SFX candidates over 156 s, mostly music beds plus chimes and reverse swooshes; a reverse-swoosh cluster (x002-x006) rides the orb transformations at 9-12 s, a reverse swoosh (x094) accompanies the giant-glyph sweep and an impact-labelled hit (x099) lands on the wordmark; integrated loudness -11.99 LUFS with a ~132.5 BPM bed. The generated voices are the hero and are left clear; many candidates are 'unsure', so exact SFX design is partly inferred.

vo_script_quality.evidence: Narration is sparse and rhythmic ('doesn't just speak, it performs', 'tone, texture, intent', 'you don't just imitate a voice, you embody it') and the demo scripts are written to show range (crying, accent switch, comic pigeon reveal, clinical call). The feature list near the end is a dense run-on sentence.

brand_consistency.evidence: The same off-white canvas, two-tone gradient orbs, grotesque sans and outlined 'V4' pill badge run from the opening disclaimer to the closing lockup, ending on the ElevenLabs wordmark.

works_muted.evidence: Muted, a viewer sees the prompts and tags typed out and the 'v4 Turbo' and logo cards, but the value (expressive voice output) is audio-only and the narrator's feature claims are not captioned.

overall.evidence: A highly polished, cohesive launch film where demos act as proof and every feature has a bespoke visual metaphor; it is held back from best-in-class as an explainer by the absence of any product surface, no CTA and weak muted comprehension.

localization_friendliness.notes: Long English prompt captions with karaoke timing are baked into the demos (s001, s005, s010; s010 also shows Chinese captions), and the feature story is carried by the voice-over and the generated audio itself; only the abstract visuals and the logo end card transfer without rework.
